reason: The Hebrew biblical text presented (Judges 6-7) demonstrates numerous instances of the Israelite people actively expressing their views and concerns. The Israelites cry out (וַיִּזְעֲקוּ) to the Lord in distress; Gideon repeatedly questions God and the angel, asking how he can save Israel and requesting signs; townspeople discuss among themselves who performed certain actions; and Joash publicly defends his son against the people's demands. God explicitly invites Gideon to speak and respond to his words. The narrative consistently portrays open communication and dialogue rather than discouragement from expression.
